title: Chile Lithium Exports Nearly Triple in Q1 2026 — Approaching $1.1B as Sector Surges
detail: Data released on May 8, 2026 showed Chile's lithium exports reached record levels in early 2026, with April lithium carbonate exports hitting $498 million and Q1 2026 lithium revenue reaching $1.108 billion — up 147.7% year-on-year. Total trade for January–April 2026 reached $69.963 billion, an 8.2% increase versus the same period in 2025. The surge was driven by the SQM–CODELCO partnership ramping production at Salar de Atacama and new output from NovaAndino Litio coming online. The boom reinforces Chile's position as the world's largest lithium reserve holder with 36% of global reserves and positions lithium as a structural second pillar of Chilean export revenue alongside copper. The Kast administration was credited with maintaining investor confidence in the sector while the prior Boric government's national lithium strategy (ENAMI majority stake in new contracts) provided the framework for the production ramp-up.

title: Codelco–Rio Tinto Strategic Partnership Targets Faster Mining Development
detail: Codelco and Rio Tinto formalized a strategic mining partnership in early 2026, with the two companies signing a Memorandum of Understanding at the BMO Global Metals, Mining & Critical Minerals Conference on February 27, 2026 that was formally ratified and extended in May 2026. The partnership focuses on accelerating project timelines, optimizing costs, and strengthening ESG integration across major Chilean mining projects. Rio Tinto committed $900 million to lithium development, with focus on the Salar de Maricunga lithium project and the Nuevo Cobre copper region. Chile's antitrust regulator (FNE) separately approved Codelco's coordination plan with Anglo American at the Andina–Los Bronces copper project, enabling joint planning and efficiency gains. Together, the partnerships mark a significant expansion of Codelco's strategic role as the state-owned company under the Kast administration moved to accelerate production expansion while maintaining the state's majority position.

media.caption: Codelco and Rio Tinto finalize $900M lithium partnership targeting Salar de Maricunga and Nuevo Cobre
